item.title: Correction · CORRECTION to the prior 'block-by-block reconciliation' pass: the owner questioned why several plan blocks (6W/6E/7W/7E, 15A/15B, 18B) weren't visible on the rendered map, which prompted an actual satellite-imagery check of those specific areas rather than trusting the prior pass's own description of itself as exhaustive. 15A/15B/18B turned out to already be covered (the visually 'empty' area there is a real surface parking lot, not a missed building). But the 6W/6E/7W/7E area had two genuine, real, significant gaps the prior automated scan had not surfaced: MB360 (1200 4th St) -- a second, ~180m-separated volume of the already-tracked MB360 development (both 701 China Basin St and 1200 4th St are used for the same marketed 'MB360' community across apartment-listing sites) -- and Sister Lillian Murphy Community (671-691 China Basin St), a 152-unit affordable housing development by Mercy Housing, celebrated in an April 2022 City/Mayor event, not previously tracked at all. Both added with real DataSF Building Footprints geometry. MB360 (1200 4th St)'s footprint originally overlapped the adjacent Mission Bay Kids' Park by 69 sq m -- trimmed to the non-overlapping remainder, same pattern as the Mission Walk/Arterra fix in the prior pass. This is a reminder that an automated footprint scan is only as complete as its own coverage-detection logic (which, as seen with the Uber and 400/410 China Basin false positives, can both over- and under-report); a direct visual spot-check against satellite imagery remains the most reliable verification and should have been part of the original reconciliation claim, not a follow-up prompted by the owner catching it.

item.title: Correction · SECOND correction pass on Mission Bay coverage claims, this time using a proper method: rather than eyeballing footprints, polygonized real city blocks from real street geometry (src/block_fit.py's load_blocks(), the same tool used elsewhere in this project to fit new features against real blocks) and computed, for every real block touching the Mission Bay boundary, what fraction of its actual building footprint area is covered by a tracked record. Of 58 real blocks with >=30% of their area inside the boundary, 33 have meaningful real building coverage (>3% of block area built); this audit found 9 of those 33 were under 50% tracked. Investigated all 9: fixed a real bug in 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard's own geometry (mission_bay_500_terry_francois.geojson) -- it had only ever captured 1 of 3 real DataSF footprint pieces sharing its mblr (the smallest, ~1172 sq m, missing ~7460 sq m of the real ~8636 sq m building), now corrected to the union of all 3; added 1401 Third Street (~222,000 sq ft office building, built 2009, tenant not identified) and the Chase Center Parking Garage (150 Warriors Way, 469,726 sq ft structure, built 2009) as new real records. Four blocks remain under 50% tracked: all are minor (building footprint under 17% of their block's area) with no address found in DataSF Assessor parcel data to identify them -- left undocumented rather than guessed, same treatment as the already-investigated 'Community Center Garage' fragment near the Rutter Community Center. This audit method (real polygonized blocks + building-footprint coverage fraction) is more rigorous than the ad hoc satellite spot-checks and footprint-distance scans used in the prior two passes and should be the standard going forward for any future Mission Bay completeness claim.

item.title: Added · Mission Bay 7E/7W spot-check (prompted by the owner asking directly about that block): matched the plan's block '7E'/'7W' label position against real street geometry (both letters resolve to the same coarse real block, since no mapped street divides them) and found a real, previously untracked building on its own standalone Assessor lot (blklot 8711227, recorded 2012) -- the Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House, 540 Mission Bay Blvd North: a 5-story, 80-room nonprofit free lodging house for families of children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital, built 2016. Identified via the DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Roll API (property_location, use code, year built, welfare exemption all cross-checked) after OpenStreetMap/Overpass lookups failed to name it -- added only once that gave a citable address and name, not from proximity alone. A second candidate found the same way, at 1600 Owens St (blklot 8709020) near block 18A/18B, turned out to be a false lead: the DataSF Assessor tax-roll lookup that identified it as 'Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices' also revealed it was already tracked as a real parcel-joined status.csv row (added in an earlier pass with more detailed sourcing than this one found) -- check_geometry_quality.py --strict caught the 3,023 sq m overlap before it was committed, and the duplicate file was removed rather than left in. This is a reminder that the real-block coverage-fraction audit method (comparing DataSF building footprints against tracked geometry) can itself under-report coverage when a real building's Assessor parcel boundary and its DataSF building-footprint outline don't line up exactly -- it found a genuine gap here, but also one false positive, and both needed the same tax-roll cross-check to resolve either way.

item.title: Added · Mission Bay Block 6E real-parcel find, prompted by the owner directly asking why the map only showed 7E and not 7W. Investigating that pushed a re-check of the plan-to-real-world transform's local accuracy: the label positions for 7E and 7W (fit from 6 control points clustered in the South campus core) drift enough this far out that the 7W label position actually lands inside a different, adjacent block's building -- 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East), a 142-unit TNDC affordable housing development (plus a manager's unit, mid-block mews of 12 townhomes/10 flats, groundbreaking reported September 2016) that was genuinely untracked. Confirmed via its own standalone Assessor parcel (blklot 8711505) and DataSF's Historical Secured Property Tax Roll; DataSF's Building Footprints layer only captures small roof-edge fragments of this building (confirmed against satellite imagery), so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly rather than the incomplete footprint layer. Added as a real status.csv row, not an approximate trace. This is a concrete instance of the known limitation already logged for the PDF-transform approach: label positions this far from the control-point cluster cannot be trusted for identifying which real building a plan label refers to without an independent check (here, the DataSF Assessor tax-roll API) -- exactly the caveat under which the transform was adopted in the first place.
